title: Algorithmic Bias & Fairness
description: Examine how training datasets reflect and amplify human historical biases, and study mathematical definitions of algorithmic fairness.

slides.title: Data Mirrors Humanity 🪞
slides.content:
# The Roots of Algorithmic Bias

Machine learning models are not objective mathematical deities; they are empirical pattern mirrors reflecting historical data.

### Primary Vectors of Bias:
* **Historical Bias:** Training data reflects societal prejudices and discriminatory practices (e.g. historical mortgage lending or hiring decisions).
* **Representation Bias:** Under-representation of certain demographic groups in training datasets (e.g. facial recognition systems trained primarily on lighter skin tones yielding 20x higher error rates on darker skin tones).
* **Proxy Variables:** Even if protected attributes (race, gender) are excluded from the dataset, the model can learn proxies like postal ZIP codes or names to reproduce discriminatory outcomes.

quizData.question: Why does simply removing a protected attribute (e.g. race or gender) from a dataset not guarantee an unbiased model?

options.text: Because algorithms automatically reverse column deletions
Because other correlated features (like zip codes or school names) act as proxy variables
Because neural networks can only output biased weights
Because loss functions require demographic inputs

quizData.explanation: Correlated variables can carry strong statistical signals for omitted protected attributes, allowing models to inadvertently reconstruct the bias.
